attributes.body_ja:
「にもかかわらず」は日本語（にほんご）の硬（かた）い文型（ぶんけい）で「(A) のに」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。この表現（ひょうげん）は「に」と「も」、五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「拘（かか）わる」（意味（いみ）：関係（かんけい）する）、そして文語（ぶんご）助動詞（じょどうし）「ず」（意味（いみ）：ない）の組（く）み合（あ）わせでできています。

この表現（ひょうげん）は普通形（ふつうけい）の動詞（どうし）、イ形容詞（けいようし）、そして名詞（めいし）と組（く）み合（あ）わせて使（つか）われることが多（おお）く、ほとんどの場合（ばあい）、ひらがなで書（か）かれます。

この表現（ひょうげん）は文字（もじ）通（どお）りには「(A) の影響（えいきょう）を受（う）けずに (B)」のような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）すと考（かんが）えることもできますが、実際（じっさい）には「のに」とほぼ同（おな）じ逆説的（ぎゃくせつてき）な意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「にも拘（かか）わらず」と「に関（かか）わらず」を混同（こんどう）しないように気（き）をつけましょう！前者（ぜんしゃ）は (B) が (A) から予想（よそう）された内容（ないよう）と異（こと）なる場合（ばあい）に使（つか）われますが、後者（こうしゃ）はただ (A) と (B) の間（あいだ）に関係（かんけい）がないことを表（あらわ）します。
attributes.body:
にもかかわらず is a formal grammar structure in Japanese used to convey that something is 'in spite of (A)', or 'despite (A)'. This pattern is a combination of に, も, the う-Verb 拘（かか）わる 'to fixate on', or 'to stick to', and the literary auxiliary verb ず, which connects with verbs in the same way, and carries the same meaning as ない.

This structure is most frequently seen connected to verbs, い-Adjectives and nouns in their standard forms. In most cases, this pattern will appear without kanji.

Literally, this phrase can be thought of as expressing 'without being affected by (A), (B)', or 'without fixating on (A), (B)'. However, it is almost always used in exactly the same way as のに 'despite'.

Caution

It is important not to get にも拘（かか）わらず mixed up with に関（かか）わらず. The former expresses 'despite', while the latter tends to be used more often for 'no matter if'.

attributes.source: A Handbook of Japanese Grammar Patterns
A Dictionary of Intermediate Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: Both くせに and にもかかわらず convey contradiction between two facts, but with different nuance and tone. くせに is a casual expression with a blaming or critical tone, e.g. 知っているくせに何で教えてくれないの？ ('You know, so why won't you tell me!?'). In contrast, にもかかわらず is a more neutral and formal way to say 'in spite of (A)', e.g. 雨にもかかわらず出かけた ('We went out despite the rain.').

attributes.body: These expressions share the verb かかわる but have opposite functions. にかかわる describes a relation or connection, often serious, as in 命にかかわる問題 (A matter of life and death). にもかかわらず is adverbial, expressing contrast or contradiction, as in 年齢にもかかわらず (Regardless of age).

attributes.body: にかかわらず means regardless of or whether or not, as in 年齢にかかわらず (Regardless of age). にもかかわらず means in spite of and highlights contradiction between expectation and reality, often with surprise, as in 雨にもかかわらず人が集まった (In spite of the rain, people gathered).

attributes.body: Both express concession but differ in tone. にもかかわらず is formal and often used in writing to highlight strong contrast or surprise, as in 雨にもかかわらず試合が行われた (The game was held despite the rain). ものの is less formal and means even though or but, as in 雨が降ったものの試合は行われた (It rained, but the game was held).

attributes.body: Both can mean regardless of, but are used differently. にもかかわらず expresses a surprising or unexpected result in spite of circumstances, as in 年齢にもかかわらず元気だ (In spite of his age, he is energetic). を問わず applies more broadly and neutrally, indicating that something holds true in all cases, as in 性別を問わず参加できる (Participation is open regardless of gender).

attributes.body: ながらも and にもかかわらず both express contradiction, but differ in nuance and usage. ながらも conveys coexisting contradictory states, e.g. '緊張しながらもわくわくしている' ('While feeling anxious, I'm also excited'). にもかかわらず means 'despite' and is used when something occurs against expectations, e.g. '雨にもかかわらず出かけた' ('He went out despite the rain').
